smallest_supported_claim: In isolated R032 Locker run c844ce63f33522f02770d171c8845552a6ea73321af8fa7a4a779955f733ecc8, native downtime equipped assigned CAMP_RESIDENT character:25 with the staged army helmet and Glock. After native save, clean exit and the declared replacement process, the same character and camp retained the helmet, wielded Glock, 15 JHP rounds in its loaded magazine and 15 in a spare compatible magazine; the displaced rebar/wearables remained on the Locker tile, one source magazine remained there, Storage contents persisted and the camp board remained usable.
causal_account: The source fixture manifest declares map-only stock of one helmet, one Glock, three Glock 15-round magazines and one 9mm stack of 30 charges. Before service the native pickup menu identified the map items and the resident was observed with CAMP_RESIDENT assigned to [162,36,0]. Through native Zone Manager and Base Missions, this run created CAMP_LOCKER and separate CAMP_STORAGE, observed 16 enabled policy slots including helmet and ranged weapon, and advanced five ordinary game minutes using the advertised wait menu/action. No staged item was manually picked up or equipped. Post-service diagnostics show the same resident wearing the army helmet and wielding the Glock with a loaded 15-round 9x19mm JHP magazine and a second 15-round JHP magazine in the jacket. A native Locker-tile pickup view shows the sharpened rebar, soccer cap, bra and wrist watch; another shows the remaining Glock magazine. The Storage-tile pickup view shows 18 listed loose/container contents, and no items were selected. The source map UI did not print the pre-service ammo stack charge count; the count of 30 comes from the bound fixture manifest, while the native after-state shows all 30 rounds in the two magazines and no loose JHP stack. The first segment native save completion was matched by the bridge, it copied the saved McWilliams world, and the second game generation independently observed the same assignment/loadout/contents without restaging. Base Missions remained available after reload. Both native game generations exited with code 0; old PID 90668 remained separate and untouched.
